newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-St George slumps 65 cents on merger.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-St George slumps 65 cents on merger.

text.p: St George Bank shares slumped 65 cents or 7.3 percent to A$8.30 around the midsession on Monday after announcing a planned merger with Advance Bank Ltd.
Advance Bank shares rose 82 cents to A$7.10 in its first trades after the announcement, but since have slipped back to A$7.00 by 12.30 p.m. (0230 GMT).
St George said it would bid a total A$7.30 per Advance share.
Advance shareholders would be offered a mixture of A$2.10 in cash, a 20 cent special cash dividend and new St George shares up to a value of A$5.00 per Advance Bank share, St George said.
Analysts said the offer valued Advance at 2.8 times net asset backing, well above the 2.0 times asset backing level at which recent Australian bank merger prices had been based.
Brett O'Donovan, a dealer specialising in bank stocks at Brisbane broker Lance Jones, said he expected St George shares to open lower because of the high offer price for Advance stock.
"Another factor is that St George shares have been inflated recently due to takeover speculation for its stock," he said.

O'Donovan said as the merger deal was partly scrip based and capped the number of shares St George would need to issue under the offer, Advance shares were unlikely to immediately reach St George's A$7.30 offer price.
